# v1.1.0-dev.104: Windows that sit flush in their panes

Pre-release off the `dev` branch. Builds on `v1.1.0-dev.103`.

Last release made docking move the real window. This one makes a docked
window stop looking like a window sitting on top of a container, and start
looking like part of it.

## Fully docked

The container's title bar has a new toggle. Turn it on and every window
inside loses its title bar and its borders, and each one fills its pane
exactly, edge to edge. The gaps between them are the container's own.

Nothing is faked and nothing is re-rendered. Each window is still the real
application, still running, still where you left it in the alt-tab order.
The container hides the real window and draws it on itself at its pane's
size, which is why typing, scrolling and video keep working in something
that has no frame of its own.

Apps that draw their own title bar inside their window, the way File
Explorer and most browsers do, are measured and cropped rather than left
with a strip of chrome showing. Explorer's is a child window and reports a
2px caption to anyone who asks the obvious question, which is why it took
its own measurement pass.

A window WLM cannot take over stays an ordinary docked window, and the
container's bar says so rather than leaving you to spot it.

### Getting back out

The same toggle puts every title bar and border back. It now carries a tint
at rest and lights up as your pointer reaches the controls, because at 9px
in the slim bar it was easy to lose.

### If WLM stops

A hidden window with no WLM to unhide it would be invisible, so this
release does not rely on a clean exit. A separate watcher restores every
held window if WLM's process dies, and WLM itself restores anything left on
that list the next time it starts. Closing a container, deleting it, or
quitting normally all put the windows back where their panes were.

## One virtual window, many profiles

A container can now be shared. Set it to a chosen list of profiles or to
all of them, and it stays one container with one layout rather than a copy
per profile. Selecting another profile in the editor no longer closes a
container a Load put on screen, since browsing the list is not undocking.

## Docking against more than one pane

Dropping a window along the shared edge of two panes now offers to put it
under both, outlined so it reads differently from dropping it under one.
Two windows of the same application can be docked into the same container,
which used to collide on identity and land both in one pane.

## Clicking a container brings its windows with it

Clicking anywhere on a container raises it and everything docked in it, in
one movement, and it has its own taskbar button. Windows also stopped
flickering and stepping backwards during a container drag, and a slow
application no longer gets called out for not fitting when it is simply
taking its time.

## Fixes

A freshly docked window used to land about 10 pixels low and jump a moment
later, because the container measured its panes against a title bar it was
about to shrink.

An Update in the editor could put back the pane layout as it was when you
selected the profile, undoing a splitter drag or a dock made since. The
layout on disk now wins.

Removing every container from a profile takes a snapshot first, so there is
a way back if it was not what you meant.

## Install

Auto-updates from dev.53 and later. Otherwise unzip and run.
